title: Security FAQ & RFP Guidance: Approved Language (2025)
author: Camila Reyes
content:
> **Archived 2025-09-10:** this page is superseded by "Security FAQ & RFP Guidance: What We Do (and Don’t) Say" and is kept for reference only.

## Purpose
This page collects the approved phrasing Sales and Solutions Engineering should use when answering Security FAQ items and RFP questionnaires. Its goal is to keep answers consistent and to avoid accidental commitments on certifications, residency, retention and security testing.

**Use it when:**
- You are filling in a security questionnaire or RFP.
- A prospect wants a one-word answer to a question that needs nuance.
- You need wording that holds across **Hosted**, **Dedicated** and **Private** deployments.

If a question isn't covered here, don't make up an answer; follow the escalation section at the bottom.

---

## Golden rules
1) **Only describe shipped capabilities.** For “when will you have X,” say: “We can share current capabilities and discuss your requirements with our team; we don’t make roadmap commitments in RFPs.”
2) **Confirm the deployment mode.** Hosted, Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) differ in many controls.
3) **No absolutes** (“never,” “always,” “guarantee,” “fully compliant”) unless the RFP library already contains approved wording.
4) **Evidence goes through process.** SOC 2 reports, pen test letters and detailed architecture material are shared via the evidence request process, normally under NDA.
5) **When a form demands a “yes,”** answer with an accurate alternate control statement and cite the exceptions policy.

---

## Approved language patterns
### 1) “Can you share your SOC 2 report?”
**Do say:** “Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 Type II report, which we share under NDA through our evidence request process.”

**Don’t say:** “We can email it today.” / “We are SOC 2 certified.” (SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a certification.)

### 2) “Do you train models on customer data?”
**Do say:** “By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts, completions, files, or embeddings to train or fine-tune foundation models. Customer content is processed to deliver the service and may be accessed by authorized staff for support, security and reliability purposes under access controls.”

**Don’t say:** “We never access customer data.” / “We don’t store any data.”

### 3) “Are you ISO 27001 certified?”
**Do say:** “Redwood is not currently ISO/IEC 27001 certified. Our controls map to ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A domains, and we can provide SOC 2 evidence under NDA.”

**Don’t say:** “We are ISO compliant.” / “We meet ISO 27001.”

---

## Topic guidance

### A) SOC 2 (Type II)
- Do say: “Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Security criterion and any additional criteria scoped in the report; available under NDA.”
- Don’t say: “SOC 2 certified,” or that it covers every product and region.
- Control mapping requests go to GRC; share only approved excerpts.

### B) ISO/IEC 27001
- Do say: “Not currently certified; we can walk through how our controls map to ISO domains such as access control, cryptography, operations security and incident management.”
- Don’t say: “ISO certified/audited,” or give a certification date.
- If a “Yes” is mandatory, use the exceptions policy plus the SOC 2 evidence path.

### C) Data residency
- Do say: “Residency depends on deployment mode and region. We support region selection for applicable workloads and can discuss EU/US requirements.” Private deployments give the most control because the customer owns the hosting boundary.
- Don’t say: “All data stays in-country, guaranteed.”
- Clarify whether the question concerns customer content, telemetry/metadata, or billing/support data. “EU-only support access” requests go to Security/GRC and Legal.

### D) Retention & deletion
- Do say: “Retention depends on deployment mode and configuration; enterprise plans have configurable retention for certain logs. We support deletion on termination or on request, per contract, with confirmation.”
- Don’t say: “Zero retention” or “deleted immediately everywhere.”
- Don't invent backup purge timelines; point to the customer-facing retention overview or escalate to GRC.

### E) Encryption and keys
- Do say: “Data is encrypted in transit with TLS and at rest with industry-standard mechanisms. Customer-managed key (CMK) or KMS options may be available in certain enterprise deployments.”
- Don’t say: “HSM everywhere” or “customers always hold the keys.”
- BYOK/HYOK questions go to Solutions Engineering + Security.

### F) Penetration testing & vulnerability management
- Do say: “Redwood conducts third-party penetration testing at least annually, along with continuous vulnerability scanning, and remediates findings according to risk-based SLAs.”
- Pen test summary letters can be shared under NDA.
- Don’t say: “We can share the full pen test report.”
- Exact tool names or remediation timelines: use RFP library ranges or escalate.

### G) Training-on-customer-data definitions
- **Customer content:** prompts, completions, uploaded files, embeddings, customer evaluation datasets.
- **Service data/telemetry:** metrics, logs, traces, operational metadata.
- Approved “model improvement” answer: “We may use aggregated, de-identified service metrics to improve performance and reliability. We do not use customer content to train foundation models by default.”
- Don’t say: “We don’t store prompts” or “we never look at prompts.”

### H) Subprocessors
- Do say: “We maintain a subprocessor list, provided through standard procurement, and assess subprocessors under our vendor risk program.”
- Don’t say: “We have no subprocessors.” Custom notice periods or audit rights go to Legal.

### I) HIPAA / BAA
- Do say: “Regulated workloads are supported through deployment and contractual controls; eligibility depends on deployment model and scope. BAA requests are reviewed by Security and Legal.”
- Don’t say: “HIPAA compliant out of the box” or promise a BAA for any use case.

### J) Air-gapped / on-prem
- Do say: “Redwood Private offers private deployment options; some customers run in isolated environments depending on architecture.”
- Don’t say: “Fully air-gapped as standard” or “no external connectivity required.” True air-gap requirements go to Solutions Engineering + Product Security PM.

### K) Audit logs and SIEM export
- Do say: “Audit logs cover key administrative and access events; export to customer SIEM/storage depends on deployment and configuration. Enterprise plans include retention options.”
- Don’t say: “We log everything” or “all events via real-time API.”

---

## Phrases to avoid
“Certified” (outside an actual in-scope certification), blanket “compliant,” “guarantee/always/never,” “meets all requirements of <framework>,” “air-gapped”/“zero trust” as shorthand, “no data stored / no logs / no access ever.”

Preferred: “supports,” “provides,” “can be configured,” “subject to contract,” “depending on deployment mode,” “under NDA.”

---

## Escalation
- SOC 2 report, pen test letters or restricted evidence → **GRC (Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter)** via the evidence request playbook.
- Contractual security commitments (BAA, breach notification, audit rights, indemnities) → **Legal (Priya Nair) + GRC**.
- Country-specific residency guarantees or “EU-only admin access” → **GRC + Security**.
- Questionnaire forces an inaccurate “Yes” → questionnaire exceptions policy, route to **GRC**.
- Roadmap / unreleased features → **Product Security PM (Ethan Brooks)**.

For urgent deals, include the exact question, required wording, deployment mode and due date/time zone when tagging reviewers.

---

## Citation guidance
- Cite the artifact and date when quoting a Redwood security statement (example: “Redwood Enterprise Security FAQ (Last reviewed: 2025-08-15)”).
- Don't quote Slack or tribal knowledge; the Security FAQ, one-pagers and RFP library are the sources of truth.
- Deviations follow the RFP approvals SOP.
